Here’s Why It Was—and Wasn’t—Worth It.   Plus, TSA might let you bring a water bottle through security, and Chelsea Handler wants you to keep your shoes on   Greetings from New York. The city is bustling with major events like the U.S. Open and Fashion Week, but it’s a somber day marking the 25th anniversary of the terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center . 

   In travel news, it wasn’t a good week to be flying to or through the United Kingdom. A major air-traffic control system issue canceled more than 2,000 flights, many of them to and from giant Heathrow in London.  

   Got TSA PreCheck? You might be able to take water bottles through security under a plan under consideration by the TSA, according to CBS. (All passengers currently may bring a frozen bottle of water through, as many of you submitted as a travel hack in response to last week’s newsletter .) 

   In loyalty news, Hyatt and Delta are teaming up , replacing Hyatt’s longtime deal with American. The companies announced few details. 

   Airlines continued to trot out 2027 Europe routes, with La Compagnie announcing service between Newark and Düsseldorf beginning in the spring. I tried the all-business class airline last year. 

   And, lastly, a quick question for you: Did a last-minute airline plane swap cost you a seat you paid for? Let me know how they handled any downgrade by replying to this email or emailing me at dawn.gilbertson@wsj.com . 

       Flying first class     There were 16 first class seats on my United Boeing 737 MAX. DAWN GILBERTSON/WSJ   First class is having a moment in the U.S. with JetBlue, Frontier and Allegiant adding the premium seats to draw big-spending travelers.

   The big three airlines have long had it, of course, and this week I was fortunate enough to fly up front on American and United for the first time. Plenty of you get upgraded there for free due to status, but I bought the tickets. 

   I flew American from Los Angeles to Chicago for an upcoming column and United from Chicago to Newark because they flashed a last-minute upgrade in the app. A head-to-head comparison is unfair due to different flight lengths and a tiny sample so here are my general hot takes:

   You can’t beat free bags, priority check-in and expedited boarding . I wasn’t the first to board on United (travelers with its Global Services and Premier 1K go first) but was pretty close. American’s setup is similar.

   The seats are a bit stiff but oh-so-roomy . I didn’t even have to put my backpack in the overhead bin and still had plenty of room to stretch out.

   Complimentary pre-departure drinks are a treat . There’s no waiting for the beverage cart half an hour or more into the flight.

   For a splurge, the longer the flight, the better. I paid $300 for the United upgrade, a deal compared with buying it outright, but it wasn’t worth it for a 90-minute flight. You’re just getting settled into the good life when it’s time to land. There was no meal service; instead, you picked from a snack basket like you find in Delta’s Comfort Plus seats. On the American flight, I got a hot meal (short ribs and mac and cheese) and a fruit and cheese plate for dessert.

   Tech issues don’t just happen in economy. The power outlet on my American flight on a 25-year-old plane was inoperable, so my laptop died halfway into the flight while I was working. I complained and got 15,000 frequent-flier miles. (There was no in-flight entertainment screen like I had on United, but that’s an issue American will gradually fix.)

   This is an edition of the WSJ Travel newsletter, a weekly source of inspiration and advice for navigating your vacations and business trips, along with the latest travel news. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here . 

       Notes From the Road ✈️     STEPHEN KREIDER YODER AND KAREN KREIDER YODER   • How these independent retirees learned to embrace group travel . 

   • The restaurant at the top of the World Trade Center changed New York, and would have turned 50 this year.

   • The NFL Down Under: How the Rams and the 49ers tackled jet lag .

   • Our China correspondent marveled at Taiwan’s temples .

       MESSAGE FROM: BARRON'S     Barron’s Energy Insider   Stay ahead of the energy market with exclusive insights, expert analysis, and real-time data delivered to your inbox every Monday morning with the Barron's Energy Insider newsletter.   Try 4 Weeks Free  >       One Good Tip 🎯   I can’t say this enough: Pay close attention when you’re booking travel. A reader searching for a one-way flight from Miami to Charleston, S.C., ended up booking through a company called Flight Network instead of directly with the airline. He was charged an extra $52.50 fee on top of his $497 American Airlines ticket. He chalked it up as “tuition” for a lesson on making sure he’s on the airline’s actual website going forward.

       Travel Math 🧮   39C   The only aisle seat available on a last-minute United flight I booked this week. (I don’t have status.) It’s in the last row and is next to the bathroom. You better believe I’m refreshing the airline’s app every hour in hopes a better seat opens up.

       And We Quote 💬   “It was hot, but that was definitely the highlight of the trip.”

   — Oregon resident John Volkoff, on visiting a tiny leather bag shop in a cave on the Greek island of Santorini during a cruise-ship stop.

       Cheers and Jeers 🤷   Big cheers to Chelsea Handler for taking up a travel etiquette cause we can probably all agree on: bare feet on planes. The comedian, who travels several times a week, appealed to airlines for a keep-your-feet-covered policy in an Instagram post to her 5.5 million followers that went viral.

   Cheers, too, to United Airlines’ unparalleled app. Ahead of my flight from Chicago to Newark Wednesday, the airline let me know the exact door at O’Hare for bag drop-off and TSA PreCheck Touchless.

   And the free Olipop sodas American Express is giving out in a to-go bin at select Centurion lounges. I stuffed one in my backpack on the way out in Phoenix on Monday and didn’t have to grab an overpriced soda at the hotel. (Don’t judge. I like soda. At least this is a prebiotic soda.)

   Jeers to hotel shuttles that take forever. I waited about 40 minutes at LAX Monday for a Hyatt House shuttle. Meanwhile, the shuttle to the nearby Hyatt Regency LAX passed by five times, with a giant sticker saying guests at the other two airport Hyatts couldn’t hop on.

       One Final Shot 📷     DAWN GILBERTSON/WSJ   Visitors to Hermosa Beach, Calif., were treated to a Labor Day rainbow on Monday.
